microtheory.name: scene_understanding
microtheory.definition: Visual understanding of complex environments. Gist, layout, navigation, spatial cognition, scene categories, context effects. Where individual objects compose into meaningful scenes. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional spatial Mt.

concepts.name: scene_gist
concepts.definition: Rapid (~100ms) category recognition. Beach vs forest vs street. Pre-attentive. Substrate analogue: substrate's coarse-classification fast path.

concepts.name: global_image_features
concepts.definition: Statistical descriptors of whole image (spatial envelope, openness, naturalness). Oliva + Torralba. Substrate analogue: substrate's image-level feature.

concepts.name: scene_categories
concepts.definition: Indoor, outdoor, urban, natural, beach, forest, kitchen, etc. ~100-1000 categories meaningful. Substrate analogue: substrate's scene-Mt categories.

concepts.name: spatial_layout
concepts.definition: Arrangement of major surfaces in scene. Ground plane, walls, ceiling. Substrate analogue: substrate's geometric scene model.

concepts.name: spatial_envelope
concepts.definition: Oliva + Torralba 2001. Holistic representation: openness, depth, naturalness, roughness, expansion. Substrate analogue: substrate's scene-shape descriptor.

concepts.name: scene_geometry
concepts.definition: 3D structure of environment. Walls, floors, support surfaces. Substrate analogue: substrate's 3D scene reconstruction.

concepts.name: context_effects_on_object
concepts.definition: Object recognition faster + more accurate in consistent scene context. Toaster in kitchen vs forest. Bar + Aminoff 2003. Substrate analogue: substrate's context-conditioned Concept activation.

concepts.name: scene_object_consistency
concepts.definition: Objects + scenes mutually predict. Toaster predicts kitchen + vice versa. Substrate analogue: substrate's mutual-prediction between Mts.

concepts.name: scene_grammar
concepts.definition: Vo + Wolfe. Implicit rules governing what objects appear where in scenes. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatial-co-occurrence pattern.

concepts.name: wayfinding
concepts.definition: Navigating from one location to another. Cognitive maps + landmark-based. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatial-graph traversal.

concepts.name: landmark
concepts.definition: Distinctive spatial reference point. Anchor for navigation. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-salience location Concept.

concepts.name: route_versus_survey_knowledge
concepts.definition: Route = sequential navigation steps. Survey = bird's-eye map. Substrate analogue: substrate's egocentric vs allocentric representation.

concepts.name: spatial_orientation
concepts.definition: Knowing where you are + facing. Vestibular + visual + proprioceptive integration. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-localization Mt.

concepts.name: cognitive_map
concepts.definition: Tolman 1948. Mental representation of environment. Allocentric. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatial-Mt for environment.

concepts.name: egocentric_frame
concepts.definition: Spatial relations relative to self (left, right, ahead). Substrate analogue: substrate's self-relative spatial encoding.

concepts.name: allocentric_frame
concepts.definition: Spatial relations relative to world (north, east). Substrate analogue: substrate's world-relative spatial encoding.

concepts.name: scene_segmentation
concepts.definition: Partitioning image into meaningful regions. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatial-Concept boundary detection.

concepts.name: figure_ground_scene
concepts.definition: Separating salient figure from background. Substrate analogue: substrate's salience-driven segmentation.

concepts.name: visual_search
concepts.definition: Finding target among distractors. Feature search (fast) vs conjunction search (slow). Substrate analogue: substrate's attention-search mechanism.

concepts.name: indoor_outdoor_classification
concepts.definition: Rapid distinction. Different statistical features. Substrate analogue: substrate's coarse-environment classifier.

concepts.name: natural_versus_manmade
concepts.definition: Statistical distinction. Natural scenes have 1/f spectral statistics; manmade more horizontal/vertical structure. Substrate analogue: substrate's natural-vs-built distinction.

concepts.name: place_cells_scene
concepts.definition: Hippocampal cells firing at specific locations in environment. Substrate of cognitive map. Substrate analogue: substrate's location-specific Concept.

concepts.name: parahippocampal_place_area
concepts.definition: PPA. Selectively responds to scenes + places, not objects or faces. Epstein + Kanwisher 1998. Substrate analogue: substrate's specialized scene-Mt.

rules.name: scene_gist_extracted_rapidly
rules.head: the substrate is briefly exposed to a complex image
rules.body: scene category is identified within ~100ms — before individual objects. Substrate's coarse-fast classification path.

rules.name: scene_context_biases_object_recognition
rules.head: the substrate sees an object in a consistent scene context
rules.body: context primes consistent categories + accelerates recognition. Bar 2003. Substrate's context-conditioned activation.

rules.name: scene_grammar_predicts_object_locations
rules.head: the substrate has seen a scene category
rules.body: implicit scene grammar predicts where specific object types appear (sink near counter, painting on wall). Vo + Wolfe. Substrate's spatial co-occurrence model.

rules.name: navigation_requires_landmarks_and_routes
rules.head: the substrate navigates an environment
rules.body: landmarks anchor location; routes connect them. Cognitive map integrates both. Substrate's spatial-graph traversal.

rules.name: natural_scenes_have_distinct_statistics
rules.head: the substrate processes natural vs manmade scene
rules.body: spatial-frequency + orientation statistics differ. Natural ~1/f. Substrate's environmental statistics.
